match.reason: The only candidate, on conjugate acid-base pairs in chemistry, is a different idea from the complex conjugate used to rationalise division in complex numbers, so no bank point teaches this point.

draft.title: Conjugates and division
card: The conjugate of a + bi is a − bi. Only the sign of the imaginary part changes.
A number times its conjugate is real: (a + bi)(a − bi) = a² + b².
To divide, multiply the top and bottom by the conjugate of the denominator. This makes the denominator real.
draft.remember: To divide, multiply top and bottom by the denominator's conjugate.

a.why: A number times its conjugate is a² + b² = 9 + 4 = 13. The option 5 comes from a sign error, treating the result as a² − b².

b.q: What is 5/(1 − 2i) in the form a + bi?
b.why: Multiply top and bottom by 1 + 2i. The bottom becomes 1 + 4 = 5, and the top is 5 + 10i, so the result is 1 + 2i. Using 1 − 2i gives the wrong sign.
b.clue: Use the conjugate 1 + 2i, then simplify by 5.

problems.detail: The why says 'Using 1 − 2i gives the wrong sign', which is unclear. Multiplying top and bottom by 1 − 2i does not give the option 1 − 2i (it gives 5(1 − 2i)/(−3 − 4i)). The option 1 − 2i really comes from flipping the sign of the result, and the why should say so.
